title: or/and and higher-order functions return Indeterminate when an earlier operand errors and a later one decides
description: Grok round 4 review (evidence/reviews/code/rv009). LogicalFunctions or/and (LogicalFunctions.java:105-111) and HigherOrderFunctions any-of, all-of, any-of-any (and all-of-any, any-of-all, all-of-all) stop at the first operand or element whose evaluation throws, so the result is Indeterminate even when a later operand is True (or) / False (and). XACML 3.0 A.3.5: or SHALL return True if at least one argument evaluates to True; and SHALL return False if at least one is False; A.3.12 combines any-of/any-of-any with or and all-of with and. Example: any-of(string-regexp-match, "[", bag(...)) style predicate error on one element, True on a later element. Behavior is pre-existing (a8a90d46 anyOf loop propagates the exception) and consistent across the engine. Decide the semantics for all six functions together (maintainer), then add tests (task 4.3) and fix in one change.

title: Temporal equality ignores timezones or compares offsets instead of instants
description: Found in rv044 (Grok): EqualityPredicates date-equal/dateTime-equal/time-equal call Value.equals. ISO8601Date parses with ISO_DATE into LocalDate and drops the zone, so 2002-10-10+14:00 equals 2002-10-10-12:00 (different days). ISO8601DateTime uses OffsetDateTime.equals, so 2002-10-10T12:00:00Z != 2002-10-10T13:00:00+01:00 (same instant); ISO8601Time equals ignores timeZoneDefined, same gap for time. XACML 3.0 A.3.1 follows XPath F&O op:date-equal, op:dateTime-equal, op:time-equal (compare after normalizing to UTC; implicit timezone for unzoned values). Check the ordering functions (less-than etc.) and date round trip (the zone must be kept).

the context (root field and DescendantEvaluationContext.evaluationStatus).

expression fails (Rule.java ~:137) or when the context is not valid
(~:111). They keep the stale missing-attribute status instead of
processing-error. Read from the code; no test shows it yet.

it to the code that catches the exception; (b) the logical and higher-order
functions restore the status of the context when a deciding value overrules
a failed operand; (c) Rule sets the status from the exception it caught.

title: Function argument count and types are not validated when a policy is loaded or evaluated
description:
Found on 2026-10-07 while fixing policy4j-the.4.53 (run 076). Read from the code; not reproduced yet.

## Observation

- `Apply(Builder)` (xacml-core `v30/policy/Apply.java` ~:62) stores the function and the arguments without a check.
- `FunctionSpec.validateParametersAndThrow` has one caller in production code: `HigherOrderFunctions.java` ~:342 (the `map` validator). No policy mapper calls it.
- `FunctionSpecImpl.invokeWithList` (`FunctionSpecBuilder.java` ~:367) validates only when `context.isValidateFuncParamsAtRuntime()` is true. `PolicyDecisionPointContextFactory` (~:80) sets `validateFuncParamsAtRuntime = false` by default.

## Expected effect (to reproduce first)

| Policy expression | Declared | Result by reading the code |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `integer-add(5)` | `@XacmlFuncParamVarArg(min=2)` | 5 |
| `integer-add()` | `min=2` | Indeterminate processing-error (`NullPointerException` in the function; kept so by run 076) |
| `string-equal("a")` | two fixed parameters | Indeterminate processing-error from the reflective call |
| `integer-add("a", 1)` | integer arguments | Indeterminate processing-error from the reflective call |

Normative basis: not fetched in this session. Before the decision, fetch what XACML 3.0 says about an `Apply` whose arguments do not match the function signature (core specification, expression evaluation and Appendix A.3) and quote it here.

## Tests to write first

1. Through `Apply.builder(id, provider).param(...).build().evaluate(context)` and through a policy loaded by the XML mapper: the four rows above.
2. Decide and pin: reject at policy load (`PolicySyntaxException` from the mapper or from `Apply.Builder.build`) or Indeterminate with status syntax-error at evaluation.

## Options

a. `Apply.Builder.build()` calls `spec.validateParametersAndThrow(arguments)`. Cost: once per policy load. Risk: policies that load today stop loading; needs the conformance run.
b. Turn `validateFuncParamsAtRuntime` on by default. Cost: one validation per function call on the decision path; needs JMH.
c. Check only the argument count at invocation.

Needs a maintainer decision between a, b, c before the fix.
close_reason: Fixed (integration/modernize-core-jdk28-valhalla, commit 'Check function arguments when an Apply is built'). title: Multiple-resources repeated-categories expansion has no bound (request-driven denial of service)
description:
Found on 2026-10-07 while fixing policy4j-the.4.50 (run 077). Read from the code; not reproduced yet.

## Code

`xacml-pdp` `v30/pdp/request/MultipleResourcesViaRepeatingAttributesHandler.handle` (~:57-75):

```java
for(CategoryId categoryId : request.getCategoriesByCategoryId().keySet()){
    ...
    byCategory.add(ImmutableSet.copyOf(attributes));
}
Set<List<Category>> cartesian = Sets.cartesianProduct(byCategory);
for(List<Category> requestAttr : cartesian){
    results.addAll(handleNext(...));
}
```

No limit on the number of repeated `<Attributes>` per category or on the product (Multiple Decision Profile, section 3.3).

## Effect

- 4 categories with 100 `<Attributes>` elements each (400 elements, a small request) expand to 10^8 individual requests.
- Above `Integer.MAX_VALUE` Guava throws `IllegalArgumentException("Cartesian product too large")` out of the handler.
- Chain order in `MultipleResourcesHandler`: request references, repeated categories, legacy XPath, XPath. The limit of policy4j-the.4.50 applies to each request that leaves this handler, so the total is (product of the repeats) x (up to 100).

## Fix shape (same as policy4j-the.4.50)

- Reuse `maxExpandedRequests` of `MultipleResourcesHandler(int, int)`: check the running product per category before `Sets.cartesianProduct`; beyond it one Indeterminate with processing-error and the fixed message `MultipleResourcesViaXPathExpressionHandler.LIMIT_EXCEEDED_MESSAGE`.
- Decide whether the limit is per handler or one budget for the whole chain (repeats x XPath paths).

## Tests to write first

1. 11 x 11 repeated categories with the default limit: one Indeterminate, zero PDP calls.
2. 10 x 10: 100 results.
3. 5 categories x 100: no `IllegalArgumentException`.
4. Repeated categories that each carry a `multiple:content-selector`: total number of PDP calls is at most the chain budget.

Needs a maintainer decision: ruling D16 names the XPath expansion only.
close_reason: Fixed in 9d6d12bc (integration/modernize-core-jdk28-valhalla). One limit (default 100) for the whole multiple-decision expansion: request references, repeated categories, individual requests that reach the selector step, evaluations, results. Evidence: openspec/changes/modernize-core-for-jdk28-valhalla/evidence/tests/081-repeated-categories-limit; review evidence/reviews/code/rv090-repeated-categories-limit-kimi (Kimi, APPROVE round 2). Implemented on the run's recommendation; the default limit is a proposal.

title: regexp-match: a pattern can make the matcher work without reading the input; that work is not stopped
description:
## Component

`xacml-core`, `org.xacml4j.v30.policy.function.impl.RegExpFunctions.matches(String, String, Limits)`.
Functions: every `*-regexp-match` (string, anyURI, ipAddress, dnsName, rfc822Name, x500Name).

## Defect

`java.util.regex` has no step budget. The time limit of bead policy4j-the.4.51 is checked in
`DeadlineCharSequence.charAt`, so it stops only work that reads the input. A pattern can make the
matcher backtrack without a call of `charAt`. That work is not stopped; the thread runs until the
match ends.

Reproduction (JDK 21.0.6, `evidence/tests/078-regexp-limits/regex-probe.txt`, probe 4):

| Pattern | Input | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `"(?:(?=)|(?=))".repeat(26) + "(?!)"` | `""` | `false` after 2,092 ms (2^26 paths, no read of the input) |
| the same with 40 groups | `""` | not run; 2^14 times longer by extrapolation (about 9.5 hours) |

The 40-group pattern has 524 characters and repetition weight 1, so the pattern-length limit
(10,000) and `repetitionWeight` (limit 1,000,000) accept it.

## What is bounded today (bead policy4j-the.4.51)

- pattern length, input length (before compilation);
- time, where the matcher reads the input (`DeadlineCharSequence`);
- nested counted repetitions `{n}` (`repetitionWeight`), the first known kind of work without a read;
- a result that arrives after the time limit is discarded (Indeterminate, processing-error). The CPU
  time is spent all the same.

## Reachability

The pattern is argument 0 of the function. It is normally a literal in the policy (trusted author).
It can be any string expression, so a policy that takes the pattern from a request attribute gives
the request control of it. No check prevents that.

## Options (maintainer decision)

| | Option | Cost |
| --- | --- | --- |
| a | Accept: a pattern is policy content. Document it. Optionally reject, at policy load, a `*-regexp-match` whose argument 0 is not a literal | policies that compute a pattern stop loading |
| b | Parse the pattern against the XPath F&O 7.6.1 grammar and reject Java-only constructs (lookaround, inline flags, `\Q..\E`, possessive quantifiers); bound the parsed tree (repetitions, alternatives that match the empty string) | own parser; patterns that rely on Java syntax become Indeterminate |
| c | Linear-time engine (RE2/J) for the match | new dependency; no back-references (`\1` is in XPath F&O 7.6.1) |
| d | Run the match on a bounded worker pool and abandon it at the time limit | an abandoned worker runs until the JVM ends; when the pool is used up every `*-regexp-match` is Indeterminate |

## Acceptance

- A test with the pattern above (40 groups) returns Indeterminate with status
  `urn:oasis:names:tc:xacml:1.0:status:processing-error` within the time limit, and no thread keeps
  running after it (not required for option a).
- `RegExpLimitsTest` and both OASIS conformance suites stay green.
- Spec delta in `specs/request-limits/spec.md` (requirement "Regular-expression matching is bounded").

## Sources

- Review `evidence/reviews/code/rv087-regexp-limits-codex`, round 2, finding 2.
- `evidence/tests/078-regexp-limits/summary.md`, section "Limits".
close_reason: Accepted as a documented limit (option a) on the run's recommendation under the maintainer's standing instruction; no separate ruling. Commit 67bfd13d (integration/modernize-core-jdk28-valhalla): class comment of RegExpFunctions; no behaviour change. Record: openspec/changes/modernize-core-for-jdk28-valhalla/evidence/builds/084-regexp-residual-accepted. This is a risk acceptance, not a fix: reopen to choose option b (own pattern parser), c (linear-time engine) or d (worker pool).

title: Integer arithmetic wraps on overflow instead of Indeterminate (ruling D4)
description:
## Component

`xacml-core`: `org.xacml4j.v30.policy.function.impl.ArithmeticFunctions` and
`org.xacml4j.v30.types.IntegerVal`.

## Defect

The integer arithmetic functions compute with Java `long` operators and wrap:

| Call | Result today | Ruled result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `integer-add(9223372036854775807, 1)` | `-9223372036854775808` | Indeterminate, processing-error |
| `integer-subtract(-9223372036854775808, 1)` | `9223372036854775807` | Indeterminate, processing-error |
| `integer-multiply(4294967296, 4294967296)` | `0` | Indeterminate, processing-error |
| `integer-abs(-9223372036854775808)` | `-9223372036854775808` | Indeterminate, processing-error |
| `integer-divide(-9223372036854775808, -1)` | `-9223372036854775808` | Indeterminate, processing-error |

A wrapped value is a wrong value that a policy then compares, so a condition can
change its result without an error.

## Ruling

Run 061 D4, option (a), accepted 2026-10-07 (`evidence/builds/070-maintainer-rulings`):
an integer result outside 64 bits is Indeterminate with status
`urn:oasis:names:tc:xacml:1.0:status:processing-error`. The plan lists the ruling
under task 5.4. This bead applies it to the current `IntegerVal` code in phase 4;
task 5.4 keeps the rest (one owner of `xs:integer`, strict integer lexing, product
identity, null stubs) and must keep these tests green on the donor types.

## Scope

- `integer-add`, `integer-subtract`, `integer-multiply`, `integer-divide`,
  `integer-mod`, `integer-abs`.
- `IntegerVal.add`, `subtract`, `multiply`, `abs`.
- A variadic call whose intermediate value leaves the range while the result is
  inside it returns the result (`integer-add(MAX, 1, -1)` is `MAX`).

Not in scope: the factories of `IntegerVal` (`of(BigInteger)`, `of(Number)`,
`ofAny(DoubleVal)`), which truncate; integer lexing; `double-to-integer`, which
already rejects values outside the range (run 072).

## Acceptance

- Rows 35 and 36 of `FunctionSafetyNet43Test` run (no `@Disabled`) and require
  processing-error.
- New boundary tests for the six functions: the largest and smallest results that
  fit, and one step beyond.
- Spec delta in `specs/function-semantics/spec.md`.
- Full reactor and conformance unchanged on JDK 21.

Ruling D4: integer-add, -subtract, -multiply, -divide and -abs are Indeterminate processing-error when the result is outside 64 bits; an intermediate value outside the range does not matter. Rows 35 and 36 of FunctionSafetyNet43Test run. Clean reactor 7,829 tests, 0 failures, 20 skipped. Review rv089 (Kimi): APPROVE in both rounds; Codex gave no report. title: XML content comparison ignores children and documents; XmlContent equals and hashCode disagree
description:
Found on 2026-10-07 while testing policy4j-the.4.57 (run 081): five repeated categories that
differed only in `<Content>` expanded to four individual requests in one test and to five in
another.

## Code

`xacml-core` `org.xacml4j.util.DOMUtil.compareNodes(Node, Node)` (~:522-592):

```java
if (expected instanceof Document) {
    ...
    compareNodes(expectedDoc.getDocumentElement(), actualDoc.getDocumentElement());  // result dropped
} else if (expected instanceof Element) {
    ... name, namespace, attributes, number of children ...
    for (int i = 0; i < expectedChildren.getLength(); i++) {
        compareNodes(expectedChild, actualChild);                                     // result dropped
    }
}
return true;
```

- Two `Document` nodes always compare as equal.
- Two `Element` nodes compare as equal when the root name, namespace, attributes and the number of
  children agree; the children themselves are not compared.

`org.xacml4j.v30.content.XmlContent`:

- `equals` is `DOMUtil.isEqual(contextNode, other.contextNode)`; `contextNode` is a `Document`, so
  any two `XmlContent` are equal.
- `hashCode` is `contextNode.hashCode()`, the identity hash of the DOM node. Equal objects have
  different hash codes.

## Effect

- `Entity.equals` and `Category.equals` include the content, so two categories with the same
  attributes and different `<Content>` are equal, with different hash codes.
- `MultipleResourcesViaRepeatingAttributesHandler` puts the categories of one id into an
  `ImmutableSet`. Observed in run 081: of five categories that differed only in content, four were
  left in one test and five in another. Assumed cause (not read in the Guava source in this
  session): the set compares with `equals` whenever two elements meet in the hash table, which
  depends on the identity hash codes. An individual request and its result are then missing from a
  multiple-decision response.
- Other hash-based uses of `XmlContent`, `Entity`, `Category` and `RequestContext` have the same
  inconsistency. Which ones exist (decision cache keys, other sets) was not checked.
- `DOMUtilTest` asserts only that equal documents are equal; no test compares different documents.

## Fix shape

- `compareNodes`: return the result of the document-element comparison and of every child
  comparison.
- `XmlContent.hashCode`: a hash that agrees with `equals` (computed from the same structure that
  `compareNodes` reads: names, namespaces, non-namespace attributes, trimmed text, children in
  order), computed once.

## Tests to write first

1. `DOMUtil.isEqual` is false for two documents that differ in a root attribute, in a child element
   name, in text, in the number of children, and in a nested child; true for documents that differ
   only in whitespace-only text nodes and in namespace prefixes.
2. `XmlContent`: equal content has equal hash codes; different content is not equal.
3. `MultipleResourcesViaRepeatingAttributesHandler`: N repeated categories that differ only in
   `<Content>` give N individual requests, for several N (the defect is non-deterministic, so repeat
   the construction).
4. Full reactor and both conformance suites: a comparison that was always true may hide other
   differences (response comparison in the conformance harness uses its own comparison; check).
close_reason: Fixed in 8baa9d42 (integration/modernize-core-jdk28-valhalla). DOMUtil.compareNodes compares the whole tree without changing it; DOMUtil.hashCode agrees with it; XmlContent uses both. Evidence: openspec/changes/modernize-core-for-jdk28-valhalla/evidence/tests/082-xml-content-equality; review evidence/reviews/code/rv091-xml-content-equality-codex (Codex, APPROVE round 3). Kept: white-space leniency of the old code. Limit: the content DOM stays reachable through toNode() and XPath results; contract documented, not enforced.

title: Dynamic type for arguments whose data type is known only at evaluation (follow-up of 4.56)
description:
Follow-up of policy4j-the.4.56 (commit dc7140f4, run 083). Plan approved by the maintainer on 2026-10-09.

## Component

`xacml-core`: `org.xacml4j.v30.policy.Apply`, `org.xacml4j.v30.types`, `policy/function` parameter
specifications, `policy/function/impl/AttributeDesignatorFunctions`, `HigherOrderFunctions`.

## Defect

Rule 2 of run 083: an argument whose type can not be told when the expression is built is a type
error. The bag of `attribute-designator` / `attribute-selector` (functions) with a data-type
argument that is not a literal is therefore unusable: every expression that takes it is
Indeterminate. The Related and Nested Entities Profile v1.0, section 6.1, makes the data type a
value of the third argument ("The value of the argument specifies the value of the DataType XML
attribute of the XACML attribute values returned by the function."), not a literal.

Second defect, found while planning: `all-of-any`, `any-of-all`, `all-of-all` have no parameter
validator. `all-of-all(string-equal, integer-bag, string-bag)` passes the check of bead 4.56, and
`all-of-all` invokes the predicate without a check of the element types.

## Change

- `DynamicType` (`enum`, implements `ValueType`, singleton): a data type known only at evaluation.
  A bag of it is `DynamicType.INSTANCE.bagType()`. No method returns null. Not in the type
  registry. `isConsistent(expected, actual)`: equal, or same shape and one side dynamic.
- The designator-function resolver returns the dynamic bag type when the data type is not a
  literal.
- Typed parameter specifications accept by consistency.
- `Apply` wraps every argument of dynamic static type in a `TypeAssertion`: the value is checked
  against its parameter when it is evaluated; a mismatch is processing-error and the function is
  not invoked.
- The three two-bag higher-order functions get the any-of-any validator; `all-of-all` checks its
  evaluated operands.

## Tests first

- `DynamicTypeTest`: consistency table, registry, `ofAny`, bag builder.
- `ApplyArgumentValidationTest`: rejected at build (shape, arity, another wrong argument, a wrong
  operand of a higher-order function); accepted at build and checked at evaluation (right and
  wrong data type); `or(true, <dynamic>)` keeps ruling D11.
- PDP and XML-mapper rows with a computed data type.

## Acceptance

- `clean verify` on JDK 21 green; conformance 937 with 12 skipped, IIC003 and IIC014 unchanged.
- Mutation check: consistency off, assertion off, `all-of-all` check off, resolver throwing.
- Spec delta in `specs/function-semantics/spec.md`; design decision in `design.md`.
- Review by another model family; evidence run 086.

title: Tighten generic bounds on ValueType.ofAny and the TypeCapability family
description:
Maintainer edits on 2026-10-24 in the integration worktree
(`integration/modernize-core-jdk28-valhalla`), plus the follow-up edits that make the reactor
compile. All uncommitted. No tasks.md entry covers this yet; the nearest task is 5.3.

## Component

- `xacml-core`: `org.xacml4j.v30.TypeCapability`, `TypeCapabilityFactory`, `types.ValueType`,
  `types.DynamicType`, `types.TypeToString`, `types.TypeFactory`.
- `xacml-json`: `TypeToGSon`.
- `xacml-xml`: `TypeToXacml30`.

## Change

- `ValueType.ofAny` (both overloads) and `DynamicType.ofAny`: `<T extends Value<?>>`. The bound
  `<T extends Value<T>>` does not compile: `Value<T>` is a `Supplier<T>`, so `T` is the payload
  type (`BooleanVal` is a `Value<Boolean>`), and inference fails at each typed call site.
- `ValueType` extends `Function<Object, Value<?>>`; `apply` returns `Value<?>`.
- `TypeCapability<T>` is self-typed: `forType`, `discoverCapabilities`,
  `AbstractCapabilityFactory`, and `TypeCapabilityFactory` take `T extends TypeCapability<T>`.
- `TypeToString`, `TypeToGSon`, and `TypeToXacml30` extend `TypeCapability<Self>`; their `Value`
  parameters and results are `Value<?>`.
- The `TypeFactory` maps are `final`.

- Full reactor `test` on JDK 21, offline, Maven 3.9.16 (bundled with IntelliJ; Homebrew Maven
  3.10 needs a plugin that is not cached): 8,009 tests, 0 failures, 0 errors, 18 skipped.
- Use sites: ripwire `uses` and `impact`, tgrep, ast-grep; the compiler checked each call site.
  Serena and the IntelliJ MCP were not available.

- OpenSpec coverage: a tasks.md entry (or a note under 5.3) and a design note, because this
  changes public API generics.
- Evidence run, review by another model family, commit by the maintainer.
- Raw `Value` locals in callers (for example `XmlContent`, `TypeToStringTest`) still compile;
  clean them up separately.
- `TypeToProto` in `xacml-proto` (not in the reactor) still uses the raw `TypeCapability`.

title: ValueType.apply passes the whole array for a one-element Object[]
description:
Found on 2026-10-24 during the review of policy4j-the.5.6. Pre-existing; that work does not
change it.

## Component

`xacml-core`: `org.xacml4j.v30.types.ValueType.apply(Object)`.

## Defect

For an `Object[]` with one element, `apply` calls `ofAny(o)` with the whole array, not with
`array[0]`. The type factories do not accept an `Object[]`: `StringVal.ofAny` throws
`SyntaxException.invalidAttributeValue`. So `apply` fails for `{"a"}` and succeeds for
`{"a", param}`.

Evidence: source reading only. Not reproduced in a test.

## Fix

- Test first: `apply` with a one-element array returns the same value as `ofAny(array[0])`.
- In the `array.length == 1` branch, call `ofAny(array[0])`.

title: 6.8 Invoke functions through MethodHandle and MethodType instead of Method.invoke
description:
OpenSpec: modernize-core-for-jdk28-valhalla, task 6.8. Requested by the maintainer on 2026-10-07.

## Current code (xacml-core, org.xacml4j.v30.policy.function)

- `FunctionInvocationFactory.Default.doInvoke`: `java.lang.reflect.Method.invoke(instance, params)` on every call. Every `Throwable` is wrapped in `RuntimeException`, so the cause chain is `RuntimeException -> InvocationTargetException -> target exception`.
- `impl/DefaultFunctionInvocation.invoke`: builds `Object[] params` (optional `EvaluationContext` first, the fixed arguments, one array for the variadic parameter), calls `PolicyToPlatformFunctionInvocation.invoke(Object...)`, and finds the first `EvaluationException` with `invocationCause()`.
- `impl/JavaMethodToFunctionSpecConverter`: calls `invocationFactory.create(instance, method)` once per function (two call sites, about lines 244-253).

## Change

1. `FunctionInvocationFactory.Default.create(instance, m)` resolves the method once:

   ```java
   MethodHandle h = lookup.unreflect(m);   // MethodHandles.publicLookup()
   if (!Modifier.isStatic(m.getModifiers())) h = h.bindTo(instance);
   h = h.asFixedArity();                    // the variadic parameter stays one array argument
   h = h.asSpreader(Object[].class, h.type().parameterCount());
   h = h.asType(MethodType.methodType(Object.class, Object[].class));
   final MethodHandle target = h;
   return params -> (T) target.invokeExact(params);
   ```

2. Signature check at registration with `MethodType`: compare `unreflect(m).type()` with `MethodType.methodType(returnType, parameterTypes)` built from the annotations (`EvaluationContext` first when `@XacmlEvaluationContextParam` is present; an array last when the function is variadic). A mismatch is a `PolicySyntaxException` when the provider is built, not at the first call.
3. Exceptions: the target exception arrives without `InvocationTargetException`. Rethrow `RuntimeException` and `Error` as they are; wrap a checked `Throwable` once. Adjust `DefaultFunctionInvocation.invocationCause` and the `FunctionInvocationException.statusFor` tests.
4. Keep the `FunctionInvocationFactory` SPI (`FunctionProviderBuilder.builder(FunctionInvocationFactory)`). Keep a reflection factory under its own name for the JMH comparison only.
5. Lookup: `publicLookup()` covers public providers. Decide for a non-public class or method: `MethodHandles.privateLookupIn(declaringClass, MethodHandles.lookup())`, or reject at provider build. Record the decision in design.md.

## Tests (write first)

- Every function of `withDefaultFunctions()` resolves to a handle when the provider is built; the count equals the registry size.
- Static provider (`fromClass`) and instance provider (`fromInstance`, `nonStaticFunctions=true`).
- Variadic: 0, 1, n arguments; fixed plus variadic; optional parameter passed as `null`; `EvaluationContext` parameter; lazy functions (`evaluateArguments=false`).
- Exceptions: an `EvaluationException` keeps its status; `IllegalArgumentException` gives processing-error; no `InvocationTargetException` in the cause chain.
- A method that the lookup cannot reach fails at provider build with the function id in the message.

## Acceptance

- No `Method.invoke` on the decision path: `rtk rg -n 'reflect\.Method|\.invoke\(instance' xacml-core/src/main` shows only the named reflection factory.
- JDK 21 reactor green; conformance counts unchanged.
- JMH `FunctionInvocationBenchmark`, reflection factory against MethodHandle factory: `integer-add`, `string-equal`, `any-of` over a 10-element bag. Needs the `xacml-jmh` module of task 9.2 (adding the module needs the maintainer's approval, docs/ai/BENCHMARKS.md).
- Reviews by two other model families; evidence indexed in evidence/README.md.

## Order

After 6.2 (the annotation renames edit the same converter). The benchmark needs 9.2.
